papers.name: Component 1: Performing
papers.covers: Non-examined assessment, marked by the school. One solo performance and one ensemble performance, totalling at least four minutes. Recorded and moderated by Pearson. 30% of the qualification, and nothing the app can revise for.

papers.name: Component 2: Composing
papers.covers: Non-examined assessment. Two compositions of at least three minutes in total: one to a Pearson brief, one free. 30% of the qualification, done in Sibelius and Cubase at this school.

papers.name: Component 3: Appraising
papers.covers: The written exam, and the only component the app covers. 40% of the qualification. Section A is worth 68 marks: six questions on six of the eight set works, a short melody or rhythm completion taken from dictation, and one question on an unfamiliar piece. Section B is worth 12 marks: an extended comparison of a set work with an unfamiliar piece from the same area of study, with the score information you need printed on the paper.

commandWords.meaning: Give the term. One mark, no explanation, no sentence.
Give a short factual answer: a key, a tempo marking, an instrument.
Pick out a feature from the extract or the skeleton score.
Say what is happening in the music using correct terms. Two or three marks, so two or three separate points.
Say what is happening and what its effect is, or why the composer did it.
Section B: write about both pieces on the same feature in the same sentence. Writing a paragraph on each separately scores badly.
Dictation: fill in the missing pitches or rhythms on the stave from the recording, which is played several times.
An effect is named; find the musical devices that produce it and say how each one does so.

assessmentObjectives.meaning: Perform with technical control, expression and interpretation. Carried entirely by Component 1, so it is earned in the practice room rather than revised for.
Compose and develop musical ideas with technical control and coherence. Carried entirely by Component 2, the two coursework compositions.
Demonstrate and apply musical knowledge: the terms, the contexts and the facts about the set works. Half of the written exam.
Use appraising skills to make evaluative and critical judgements about music: analysing what you hear and comparing pieces. The other half of the written exam, and where the top marks are.

grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: The exact term, spelled correctly: syncopation, pizzicato, ritardando, plagal cadence. No sentence, no hedging.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Describe the texture or the harmony (2 to 3 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: One precise point per mark, each using a technical term rather than a description in ordinary words. Homophonic with a walking bass, not just the instruments and the tune.
The rhythm sketched on the first hearing and the pitches filled in on later ones, with the given bars used to fix the key and the pulse before writing anything.

grade9ByQuestionType.questionType: Explain how the composer creates an effect (4 to 6 marks)
grade9ByQuestionType.looksLike: Named devices tied to their effect: the effect, the device that causes it, and where in the extract it happens, rather than a list of features with no consequence.

Organised by musical element, not by piece: one paragraph on melody covering both pieces, one on rhythm, one on texture. Uses the skeleton scores as evidence with bar numbers, and reaches a judgement about the effect of the differences rather than only listing them.
Places the piece in its time and purpose, and links the context to something audible: a harpsichord continuo because it is Baroque, a multitracked vocal because it is a 1974 studio recording.
